content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"'Works of the law' denotes deeds performed in obedience to the Mosaic law (with debate over whether this means the whole Torah, Jewish boundary markers like circumcision/food laws/Sabbath, ceremonial prescriptions only, or human moral effort generally), which Paul denies can justify a person before God; justification is by faith, not these works. No settled consensus exists on the phrase's precise scope, but all major readings assume it picks out some identifiable class of deeds.","book_summary":"The phrase is Paul's designation for deeds considered in relation to law, with no single unchanging class of deeds as its referent: context may identify God's law, a circumcision-party application, or leave the acts unnamed. What is constant is not the deeds but the rejected claim made for them—that they can purchase justification, produce the Spirit, establish covenant standing, or place God in debt. The phrase functions as a denial of the deeds as purchase price, not as a fixed category label.","consensus_core_identification":"A determinate class of law-related deeds (Mosaic observance, boundary markers, ceremonial works, or human effort—scope contested) that Paul rejects as a means of justification.","book_core_identification":"A context-variable designation for whatever deeds are in view, unified not by the deeds themselves but by the rejected transactional claim: that such deeds can purchase justification, the Spirit, or covenant standing.","core_relation":"COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"Every consensus position (traditional Protestant, New Perspective, Catholic ceremonial-law, general-merit) assumes the phrase names one stable class of deeds and then debates which class. The book rejects that shared premise: it denies any unchanging extension, allowing the referent to shift per passage (God's law in Romans, circumcision-party demands in Galatians, unnamed pursuit in Rom 9:32). It also explicitly denies the phrase is a synonym for obedience, which cuts against the common gloss 'deeds done in obedience to the Mosaic law.' It thus absorbs multiple consensus alternatives as context-specific instances while refusing to privilege any one as the fixed meaning.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"The book retains the consensus's general category—law-related deeds Paul denies as the basis of justification—and retains the functional theological point on which all consensus readings agree (these works cannot justify). So the core is not replaced; there is compatible overlap. But the book materially changes the precision and extension: instead of adjudicating among fixed-referent options, it reclassifies the phrase as having a variable, context-supplied referent unified only by the denied transactional claim. This reclassifies cases across the consensus alternatives (each becomes locally correct rather than definitionally correct) and rejects the shared assumption of a single unchanging class, including the equation with 'obedience.' That is a real boundary-level disagreement without contradiction of the central referent, which fits REFINED. Response B's note that the scope may be 'some combination' gestures toward this, but no consensus response articulates the book's context-relative, claim-centered account as its primary meaning.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue MATCH: all three responses already deny settled consensus and list multiple scope options, and the book's 'context decides' move merely restates that interpretive plurality rather than materially disagreeing with any consensus claim; the shared theological core (works of the law cannot justify) is identical.","confidence":"medium"}
